A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ a \\ b\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}c \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $a+3b+c?$" :question/worked-solution "The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -6 & -4 \\ -6 & 6 & 4 \\ -4 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -6 & -4 & 2 \\ -6 & 6 & 4 & -2 \\ -4 & 4 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & 4 & -4 \\ -6 & 6 & 4 & -2 \\ 6 & -6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ -6 & 6 & 4 & -2 \\ 6 & -6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+6{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{3}=-2,
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+(-2)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-1+{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+3b+c=0+3\cdot (-2)+1=-5.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-bf2aa749-d040-57c2-b657-f15f0f4f8d98"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-bf2aa749-d040-57c2-b657-f15f0f4f8d98" :answer-field/id #uuid "bf2aa749-d040-57c2-b657-f15f0f4f8d98" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-985ff754-4000-553d-84fd-3adae2a90775" :answer-field/choices ["answer-a0f160c1-cc03-5355-b516-d2d19b494551" "answer-985ff754-4000-553d-84fd-3adae2a90775" "answer-fe32f448-8a3a-522b-9c2c-5ad76f739b65" "answer-612c1237-1d75-5779-901e-394b60ae8abc" "answer-b6774fe7-0b94-51e6-8366-d780b5d12442"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a0f160c1-cc03-5355-b516-d2d19b494551" :answer/id #uuid "a0f160c1-cc03-5355-b516-d2d19b494551" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-985ff754-4000-553d-84fd-3adae2a90775" :answer/id #uuid "985ff754-4000-553d-84fd-3adae2a90775" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fe32f448-8a3a-522b-9c2c-5ad76f739b65" :answer/id #uuid "fe32f448-8a3a-522b-9c2c-5ad76f739b65" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-8" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-612c1237-1d75-5779-901e-394b60ae8abc" :answer/id #uuid "612c1237-1d75-5779-901e-394b60ae8abc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b6774fe7-0b94-51e6-8366-d780b5d12442" :answer/id #uuid "b6774fe7-0b94-51e6-8366-d780b5d12442" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-d4a26f8e-8621-57f0-b0fb-289f901931d0" :question/id #uuid "d4a26f8e-8621-57f0-b0fb-289f901931d0" :question/math-academy-id "q-136954" :question/problem "$$

{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-5\end{aligned}

what is the value of $12a+\frac{b}{c}?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -18 \\ -18 & 54\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 & -10 \\ -18 & 54 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{5}{3}+3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3}+3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
12a+\frac{b}{c}=12\cdot (-\frac{5}{3})+\frac{3}{1}=-17.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-ed476833-2f74-5fd6-89de-22e15124bc5f"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-ed476833-2f74-5fd6-89de-22e15124bc5f" :answer-field/id #uuid "ed476833-2f74-5fd6-89de-22e15124bc5f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-a0ae1013-f366-5e65-90ff-b5b5ec91675a" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3394fe0c-1ef5-5d2a-acd6-6a75d0644ea8" "answer-796589ac-95c1-56f9-b1db-31d0e03ed1d4" "answer-a0ae1013-f366-5e65-90ff-b5b5ec91675a" "answer-f6952c2b-bc0a-5679-9e51-c3da4a58655d" "answer-0aa14c10-e738-56f6-ba1c-e071a121f17f"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3394fe0c-1ef5-5d2a-acd6-6a75d0644ea8" :answer/id #uuid "3394fe0c-1ef5-5d2a-acd6-6a75d0644ea8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-10" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-796589ac-95c1-56f9-b1db-31d0e03ed1d4" :answer/id #uuid "796589ac-95c1-56f9-b1db-31d0e03ed1d4" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-12" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a0ae1013-f366-5e65-90ff-b5b5ec91675a" :answer/id #uuid "a0ae1013-f366-5e65-90ff-b5b5ec91675a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-17" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f6952c2b-bc0a-5679-9e51-c3da4a58655d" :answer/id #uuid "f6952c2b-bc0a-5679-9e51-c3da4a58655d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-19" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0aa14c10-e738-56f6-ba1c-e071a121f17f" :answer/id #uuid "0aa14c10-e738-56f6-ba1c-e071a121f17f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "13" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-4a92698e-17e4-57b8-8191-7aa9adc0e63f" :question/id #uuid "4a92698e-17e4-57b8-8191-7aa9adc0e63f" :question/math-academy-id "q-137092" :question/problem "$$

what is the value of $6a+\frac{4b}{c}?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}24 & -12 \\ -12 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & 4 \\ -12 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
6a+\frac{4b}{c}=6\cdot \frac{1}{6}+\frac{4\cdot \frac{1}{2}}{1}=3.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-a27c023d-32d0-5cf3-ade4-1f1674089f41"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-a27c023d-32d0-5cf3-ade4-1f1674089f41" :answer-field/id #uuid "a27c023d-32d0-5cf3-ade4-1f1674089f41" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-8cd78f8e-e662-5c98-aa4d-0c408cd252ed" :answer-field/choices ["answer-29e85101-f9b2-5d74-83c6-aabdd8fc2745" "answer-2ccd28ea-578f-5414-8332-a6408e6df178" "answer-2baff1db-5ead-50b2-af5a-abe277ae4820" "answer-8cd78f8e-e662-5c98-aa4d-0c408cd252ed" "answer-2e8878bb-5944-584d-9b48-2add56ecc5fb"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-29e85101-f9b2-5d74-83c6-aabdd8fc2745" :answer/id #uuid "29e85101-f9b2-5d74-83c6-aabdd8fc2745" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2ccd28ea-578f-5414-8332-a6408e6df178" :answer/id #uuid "2ccd28ea-578f-5414-8332-a6408e6df178" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2baff1db-5ead-50b2-af5a-abe277ae4820" :answer/id #uuid "2baff1db-5ead-50b2-af5a-abe277ae4820" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8cd78f8e-e662-5c98-aa4d-0c408cd252ed" :answer/id #uuid "8cd78f8e-e662-5c98-aa4d-0c408cd252ed" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2e8878bb-5944-584d-9b48-2add56ecc5fb" :answer/id #uuid "2e8878bb-5944-584d-9b48-2add56ecc5fb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-abb758c7-4ff1-5d36-aa75-96f61271e2e1" :question/id #uuid "abb758c7-4ff1-5d36-aa75-96f61271e2e1" :question/math-academy-id "q-137094" :question/problem "$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

17592186134698 :step/content {:db/id 17592186135060 :tutorial/content "Let's consider the following inconsistent system of equations:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the system is inconsistent, we cannot find an exact solution. However, as we've previously seen, we can attempt to find the so-called least-squares solution, which is a vector ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ such that

$$
\|  A{\hat{\mathbf{x}}} - \mathbf{b} \|
$$

is as small as possible. 

As before, the least-squares solution can be found by solving the corresponding normal equation, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, note the following: 

- Previously, we solved the normal equation by left-multiplying the normal equation by $(A^T A)^{-1}.$

- However, in this case, the second column of $A$ is a multiple of the first.

- So, the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent.

- Therefore, $A^T A$ is not invertible.

To solve the normal equation in this case, we proceed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5 & -20 \\ -20 & 80\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the last equation by Gaussian elimination, we obtain the general solution

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1+4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that our solution is not unique! The second term of the least-squares solution (highlighted in blue) represents vectors from the null space of $A.$

Since the system is inconsistent, we cannot find an exact solution. However, as we've previously seen, we can attempt to find the so-called least-squares solution, which is a vector ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ such that

$$
\|  A{\hat{\mathbf{x}}} - \mathbf{b} \|

As before, the least-squares solution can be found by solving the corresponding normal equation, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, note the following: 

- Previously, we solved the normal equation by left-multiplying the normal equation by $(A^T A)^{-1}.$

- However, in this case, the second column of $A$ is a multiple of the first.

- So, the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent.

- Therefore, $A^T A$ is not invertible.

To solve the normal equation in this case, we proceed as follows:

$$

$$

Solving the last equation by Gaussian elimination, we obtain the general solution

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1+4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that our solution is not unique! The second term of the least-squares solution (highlighted in blue) represents vectors from the null space of $A.$

A robust knowledge of set theory is another cornerstone of mathematical proof-writing. Students will extend and formalize their understanding of sets and learn to translate between logical and set operations. By the end of the course, students will appreciate how set theory provides a comprehensive toolkit for proving mathematical results.
After mastering these fundamentals, students will explore various proof-writing techniques, including direct proof, proof by cases, proof by contrapositive, proof by contradiction, disproof, and mathematical induction. The course emphasizes proving concepts related to parity, divisibility, congruence, sequences, functions, set identities, and relations. Students will have multiple opportunities to test and refine their proof construction and comprehension skills throughout the course and in varied contexts

"Let's consider the following inconsistent system of equations:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the system is inconsistent, we cannot find an exact solution. However, as we've previously seen, we can attempt to find the so-called least-squares solution, which is a vector ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ such that

$$
\|  A{\hat{\mathbf{x}}} - \mathbf{b} \|
$$

is as small as possible. 

As before, the least-squares solution can be found by solving the corresponding normal equation, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, note the following: 

- Previously, we solved the normal equation by left-multiplying the normal equation by $(A^T A)^{-1}.$

- However, in this case, the second column of $A$ is a multiple of the first.

- So, the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent.

- Therefore, $A^T A$ is not invertible.

To solve the normal equation in this case, we proceed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5 & -20 \\ -20 & 80\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the last equation by Gaussian elimination, we obtain the general solution

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1+4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that our solution is not unique! The second term of the least-squares solution (highlighted in blue) represents vectors from the null space of $A.$ 

In general, if a matrix $A$ has collinear columns, then the least-squares solution to $A\mathbf x = \mathbf b$ is not unique." 17592186045417] [17592186135060 1065 3637 17592186045417] [17592186135060 1066 #uuid "2f2e227a-264e-5e00-8c12-ea534f4b351f" 17592186045417] [17592186135060 1067 "Introduction" 17592186045417]]}
